items.text: One round before we eat — one sentence each
“Where has your card held, or where has it slipped?”
Both answers are welcome — a slip you noticed is the practice working, because noticing is the skill
No fixing, no advice — a parent starts; pass-anytime holds
“The card is a long walk; sixteen days in, everyone in this circle is still on it.”
Luke is describing the very first church — the most spiritually alive room in the history of the world
The first church ran on two rails: the teaching, and the table
We have given fifteen weeks to the first rail — tonight is the second
“Breaking bread with glad and generous hearts is not the break between the formation — it is the formation.”
The grace — then: eat

panel.label: ACTS 2:46 (ESV)
lines: “And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts.”

items.text: Real food, no agenda — no devotional between courses, no teaching moment
“We are going to eat together. That's it. That's the session.”
Phones silenced and put away — the people at your table tonight are the evening
Dessert is held back — dessert arriving is the signal the cards are coming
A small stack on your table — someone reads the first card aloud; a parent answers first, every table, every card
Then anyone who wants to answers, in any order — nobody has to. When the card feels done, read the next one
One footprint — “Looking back at this past month — one place you can see God's hand more clearly now than you did at the time.”
Where you came alive — “What activity, conversation, or work this season has made you most alive? Why?”
The ten-year question — “What's one thing you hope is still true between us in ten years?”
No report-out — what is said at your table stays at your table. Ten minutes of laughing at your dad's answer is not a failure of the exercise — that IS the exercise
The Quarterly Pulse, third one this year — one page, three questions, about five minutes, at home
Presence — how present have I actually been in these sessions this quarter? Not attendance, presence (1–10, and one sentence why)
Surprise — one thing that has surprised me this quarter — about myself, about God, or about someone in this room
Steering — one specific way I want to engage differently in the final quarter
“This room steers by these pages” — the final quarter, the consolidation weeks and the two commissionings, is shaped by what you write
Back next Wednesday, in the bin at the door — signed or unsigned, your choice; nobody watches the bin
